findings.title: CronJob runs pile up
findings.cause: CronJob report has 3 Jobs running at once (report-29919443, report-29919444, report-29919445): its concurrencyPolicy is Allow, and each run takes longer than the schedule "* * * * *" leaves, so every new run starts beside the ones still going; the oldest, report-29919443, has run for 2m31s

evidence.what: CronJob report has concurrencyPolicy Allow and 3 active Jobs
evidence.command: kubectl get cronjob report -n kd-cronjob-runs-pile-up -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}{" "}{.spec.concurrencyPolicy}{" "}{.status.active[*].name}'

findings.fix: Set concurrencyPolicy: Forbid (skip a run while one is going) or Replace (stop the old run), and give the Job an activeDeadlineSeconds; or schedule it less often than a run takes.
